newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 29.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the UNDP will provide technical assistance to strengthen the supervisory role of the Securities and Exchange Commission.
The Board of Investment will open a desk in its premises exclusively for Korean investment.
U.S. oil company Occidental will compensate families and tea gardens affected by the gas field fire in northeast Maulavibazar district.
Malaysia said it would protect the legitimate interests of Bangladeshi workers employed in the country.
Commerce and Industries Minister Toafel Ahmed on Monday said a new industrial policy would soon be announced.

Sramik Karmachari Oikya Parishad (SKOP), an alliance of trade unions, will observe a 24 strike across the country beginning on Wednesday morning to press its demands including higher wages and suspension of disinvestment process.
Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria has said corruption in approval of bank loans and in loan recovery will not be tolerated.
Bangladeshi frozen foods exporters are frequently receiving faxes from their European buyers, expressing unwillingness to accept further supply from Bangladesh. REUTER
